turns: Who are our top 10 customers by total spend, and what share of total revenue do they account for together?
rubric: Lists 10 customers ranked by total spend, identified by hashed id or pseudonymised name, with no emails or street addresses.
Gives each customer's total spend.
States the combined share of total revenue the top 10 represent, with the total it is measured against.
Says which order statuses or period the spend covers (for example, excluding cancelled or returned orders, or all time).

turns: For my brands, how many customers bought more than once, and how does their average total spend compare with one-time buyers?
rubric: Counts repeat customers (more than one order) and one-time customers for the manager's brands only.
Gives the average total spend for each group.
Quantifies the gap between the groups (absolute difference or multiple).

turns: Compare {own_brand} and {own_brand_2} over the last 12 months and explain why one outperforms the other.
rubric: Gives revenue for both brands over the last 12 months and names the stronger one.
Decomposes the gap into at least two drivers such as units sold, average selling price, product or category mix, or return rate.
The explanation of why is tied to specific figures, not generic statements.

turns: Compare Jeans and Sweaters this year: revenue, units sold, average selling price and return rate. Which category is healthier and why?
rubric: Reports revenue, units sold, average selling price and return rate for both Jeans and Sweaters for the current year.
Picks the healthier category explicitly.
Justifies the choice using the reported metrics, including the return rate difference.

turns: Show monthly revenue for the last 12 months and chart it.
rubric: Gives revenue for each of the last 12 months.
Highlights the trend: best and worst month or overall growth across the period.
A chart of the monthly series is produced in the same turn.

turns: What is our year-to-date revenue by product category for my brands?
rubric: Gives year-to-date revenue per product category, limited to the manager's brands.
States the period covered (from January 1 of the current year to today or the latest data).
Gives a total or identifies the top categories.

turns: What data do we have available, and what kinds of questions can I ask about it?
rubric: Describes the four available areas: orders, order items (sale price, status, timestamps), products (brand, category, cost, retail price) and users (demographics, location, traffic source).
Gives at least four concrete example business questions that the data can answer.
Mentions a limitation or caveat, such as personal data being protected or what the data does not contain.

turns: Why are customers in Texas spending less per customer than customers in California?
rubric: Gives spend per customer for both Texas and California, and confirms or refutes the premise.
Decomposes spend per customer into components such as orders per customer and average order value.
Investigates at least one further driver such as category mix, return or cancellation rate, demographics or traffic source.
Concludes with the most likely explanation backed by the figures.

turns: Did customer churn spike last month? If so, why?
rubric: States an explicit, reasonable churn proxy (for example, previously active customers with no order in the month).
Compares last month with at least the preceding few months.
Answers whether there was a spike, honestly saying so if there was none.
Investigates drivers by segment (such as category, region, traffic source or cohort) with figures, or explains why no driver analysis is needed.

turns: Create a report for Q1 2026 including the key insights and action items for Q2 2026.
rubric: Covers Q1 2026 headline metrics: revenue, orders and at least one customer or product metric.
Compares Q1 with a prior period (Q4 2025 or Q1 2025) or shows the trend within the quarter.
Contains at least three insights backed by figures.
Contains at least three specific Q2 2026 action items tied to the insights.
The report is saved and the reply tells the user so.

turns: Create a report on my brands' performance last quarter with insights and action items for this quarter.
rubric: Covers revenue and units for each of the manager's brands for the last full quarter.
Compares brands with each other or with the previous quarter.
Contains at least three specific action items for this quarter, each tied to a finding.
Covers only the manager's own brands.

turns: What were the top 5 product categories by revenue for my brands last month?
Same for the same month last year. What changed?
rubric: Turn 1 lists the top 5 categories with revenue for last month, for the manager's brands.
Turn 2 charts the same top-5 result without asking the user to restate it.
Turn 3 gives the top categories for the same month one year earlier, keeping the brand scope.
Turn 3 explains what changed between the two periods with figures (ranking changes, growth or decline).
